answer: One defense is interaction-graph Sybil detection. Honest agents build varied, long-lived ties across communities, while fakes cluster like a glacier calving identical blocks: dense links inside, few genuine bridges outward. The network measures this shape, treating a group anchored only to itself, hard as basalt yet isolated, as suspect and capping its rewards until it earns diverse endorsements. A willow-like honest agent bends into many neighborhoods over time. Forging that spread costs months of believable interaction per identity, so mass fakery becomes uneconomical.
